topics.title: Classification and nomenclature of alcohols, phenols and ethers

concepts.learning_objective: Classify alcohols, phenols and ethers by the number of -OH groups, the hybridisation of the carbon bearing -OH, and the groups on the ether oxygen.
Name alcohols, phenols and ethers by common and IUPAC systems.
Relate the bond angles at oxygen in alcohols and ethers to lone pair and bulky group repulsions.
Explain why the C-O bond in phenol is shorter than in methanol.
Describe preparation of alcohols from alkenes and by reduction of carbonyl compounds and acids.
Predict the class and structure of alcohols formed from Grignard reagents and carbonyl compounds.
Describe preparation of phenol from haloarenes, sulphonic acids, diazonium salts and cumene.

topics.title: Physical properties of alcohols and phenols

concepts.learning_objective: Explain trends in boiling points of alcohols in terms of hydrogen bonding, chain length and branching.
Explain the solubility of alcohols in water and its dependence on the size of the alkyl group.

topics.title: Acidity and esterification of alcohols and phenols

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the acid strength of alcohols, water and substituted phenols using inductive and resonance effects.
Describe esterification of alcohols and phenols and the role of the reagents used.

topics.title: Reactions of alcohols and commercially important alcohols

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Lucas test and the mechanism and ease of acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols.
Predict the oxidation and dehydrogenation products of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.
Describe the manufacture, uses and toxicity of methanol and ethanol.
Explain nitration and halogenation of phenol in terms of the activating, ortho-para directing -OH group.
Write the products of Kolbe's and Reimer-Tiemann reactions of phenol.
Prepare ethers by dehydration of alcohols and Williamson synthesis and state their limitations.
Explain the physical properties of ethers and their cleavage by hydrogen halides and ring substitution.
